source_title: Proposition de résolution appelant à un moratoire sur les projets de centres de données non souverains, n° 3293
exact_quote: Enregistré à la Présidence de l’Assemblée nationale le 13 octobre 2026.

corrections.evidence: Both the resolution and the Assembly’s legislative history date the filing to October 13. The history records its introduction: https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/dossiers/moratoire_centres_donnees_non_souverains

not_confirmed: The resolution names individual Ecologist and Communist signatories. I could not confirm formal endorsements by both parliamentary groups as bodies.
notes: Ruffin proposed a five-year pause covering foreign sponsors, foreign end users and other sovereignty concerns, criticized the electricity tax break, and subsequently announced his withdrawal from the presidential race on November 22: https://francoisruffin.fr/presidentielle-2027-face-au-risque-du-pire-je-retire-ma-candidature/

source_title: Testimony of Jocelyn Benson, Michigan Secretary of State, Before the U.S. Senate Committee on Rules and Administration
exact_quote: the first election cycle where Artificial Intelligence will be used to amplify and expand exponentially these tactics and their impact
notes: The preceding sentence identifies the tactics as election misinformation and disinformation intended to confuse voters and obscure the voting process.

source_title: Fact check: John James, Jocelyn Benson debate data centers, tariffs, more
exact_quote: The moratorium should be imposed on Lansing, not the people.

corrections.correct: Attribute this wording to James’s remarks to reporters after the October 6 debate.
corrections.evidence: Bridge Michigan places the quotation in the post-debate exchange where James rejected a statewide block. WDIV records the debate wording as “My moratorium is local led, not Lansing led.” https://gmg-wdiv-prod.cdn.arcpublishing.com/news/local/2026/10/07/benson-james-offer-contrasting-visions-in-first-michigan-governor-debate/

not_confirmed: Whether James also used the exact post-debate wording onstage.
notes: No official transcript of the post-debate exchange was located, so the attribution uses the reporter’s direct account.

source_title: Terms of Engagement for Data Centers
exact_quote: Data centers must pay for their own energy demand — costs cannot be passed onto ratepayers.
not_confirmed: Whether El-Sayed also called for federal standards and interim state and local moratoriums on January 8. The campaign document omits those positions, and the supplied Michigan Advance page did not open.
notes: The January platform confirms closed-loop cooling and penalties for failing to deliver promised local jobs, while his September 15 FOX 2 interview and WCMU’s account document the later federal and moratorium positions: https://www.fox2detroit.com/video/fmc-icu8s3w75a8b6co0 and https://www.wcmu.org/local-regional-news/2026-10-01/rogers-and-el-sayed-disagree-on-many-issues-except-data-center-moratoriums

source_title: Governor Greg Abbott’s letter to Chairman Thomas Gleeson and Chief Executive Officer Pablo Vegas
exact_quote: verification and audit of all data centers advancing through ERCOT’s interconnection process before any additional data centers are approved to move forward.
not_confirmed: That critics specifically identified many mid-size projects as exempt. The letter gives no size cutoff, and the critic’s statement identifies off-grid projects as the gap.
notes: Abbott directed the PUCT and ERCOT to examine electricity and water use, and Public Citizen’s August 3 statement confirms the absence of a deadline and explains how projects generating their own power could bypass the pause: https://www.citizen.org/news/abbotts-latest-data-center-declaration-is-a-faux-pause/

source_title: Paxton promises to ban Chinese technology and chatbots that endanger children in data center platform
exact_quote: hold companies criminally liable if their data centers power AI chatbots that endanger children

corrections.evidence: The Texas Tribune reported the rollout on Monday, August 24. August 25 is the publication date of the supplied Breitbart follow-up.

notes: Paxton’s original X post would not open, so the four-point plan, proposed Chinese-technology ban, company liability and support for Abbott’s state measures were checked against contemporaneous reporting: https://texaspolitics.com/2026/08/25/ken-paxton-unveils-texas-first-data-center-plan/

source_title: James Talarico calls for tighter regulations on data center development
exact_quote: strikes a balance between welcoming those investments while also protecting working people.
notes: The July 22 video would not open, so the wording was checked against the Tribune’s direct quotation from Talarico’s Austin news conference, where he proposed federal minimum standards, local approval authority and developer-paid grid costs.

source_title: Bill History: Proposed H.B. No. 5926 — An Act Implementing a Surcharge on Electricity Consumed by Data Centers
exact_quote: 01-22-2025 REFERRED TO JOINT COMMITTEE ON Energy and Technology Committee
notes: Democratic Rep. Brandon Chafee introduced the surcharge to offset residential customers’ Combined Public Benefits Charge, and the bill history ends at referral, so June 4 marks expiration at adjournment without a defeat vote; the supplied PDF host failed, but the Assembly’s copy and adjournment record opened: https://www.cga.ct.gov/2025/agn/pdf/2025AGN00721-R01-AGN.pdf

source_title: Bill History: Substitute for Raised S.B. No. 1292 — An Act Requiring a Study Concerning Energy Efficiency Requirements for Artificial Intelligence Data Centers
exact_quote: 04-07-2025 FAVORABLE REPORT, TABLED FOR THE CALENDAR, SENATE

corrections.correct: The bill reached the Senate calendar on April 7 as Calendar No. 303, File No. 538. It expired without a floor vote when the regular session adjourned June 4, 2025.
corrections.evidence: The bill history records no action after the April 7 calendar placement, and the Senate’s reconvening agenda confirms the June 4 adjournment: https://www.cga.ct.gov/2025/agn/pdf/2025AGN00721-R01-AGN.pdf

notes: The supplied PDF host failed, but the Assembly’s bill history and File No. 538 opened and confirm that the Energy and Technology Committee approved the substitute energy-efficiency study 24–0 on March 18: https://www.cga.ct.gov/2025/FC/PDF/2025SB-01292-R000538-FC.PDF
